title: Usage export eligibility checklist + triage-bot integration for console requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a lightweight, auditable eligibility checklist (questionnaire + heuristic rules) for incoming console usage/export/dashboard requests and wire it to a Slack/Console triage-bot that classifies requests into delivery lanes (self-serve, concierge, engineering intake). The checklist should capture sensitivity, export frequency, sample size, cost sensitivity, SLA need, and dataset residency. Outcome: faster, consistent prioritization decisions and automated routing to appropriate teams with linked evidence for audits.
acceptance_criteria: A web-accessible eligibility checklist form embedded in Console request flow that saves responses to the intake ticket
A triage-bot integration (Slack + Console notifications) that ingests checklist output and posts recommended lane with rationale and links
Heuristic rule set implemented (as markdown rules) covering at minimum: PII presence, token-volume estimate, export cadence, SLA requirement, cross-tenant joins
Routing matrix that maps checklist outcomes to lanes: self-serve, analytics concierge, eng backlog, legal review
Audit trail visible on ticket showing checklist results, bot recommendation, and final human decision
Pilot with 3 enterprise customers and measurement plan to show median triage time reduced by >=40%
Documentation (Confluence) and short training playbook for CS and Solutions teams
steps: Draft initial checklist questions with CS and Solutions (focused interview: 5 customers)
Design lightweight UI mock in Figma and review with Console UX - link in comments
Implement backend schema for checklist answers (simple key-value) and attach to ticket metadata
Author heuristic rule set and unit tests (ENG) - store as markdown + YAML flags
Build triage-bot: subscribe to new tickets, evaluate rules, post recommendation to ticket thread and to Slack channel
Run closed beta for two weeks with internal triage team, iterate rules
Open pilot to 3 enterprise customers, collect metrics, finalize rollout plan
notes: This ticket intentionally keeps checklist small (10-14 questions) to avoid friction. We can iterate and add conditional questions.
Aim is not to fully automate decisions; bot provides recommended lane and rationale. Final routing must remain editable by human operators.
Consider storing token-volume estimate as both user-supplied and model-estimated (post-submit) to refine heuristics over time.
We should surface cost-sensitivity flags to Redwood Optimize so we can later offer quantization/batching recommendations tied to request lanes. Engineering dependency noted.
Legal/Privacy review gating: if PII/residency flagged => route to Security & Compliance for review before scheduling delivery. This is a hard gate in the routing matrix.
metrics_and_eval: Primary metric: median time from ticket creation to lane assignment
Secondary: % tickets auto-classified vs required human override
Pilot targets: reduce triage latency by >=40%, maintain <=10% false-positive legal escalations
risks: Overfitting rules to pilot customers causing misclassification at scale
Checklist friction leading to lower completion rates and noisy signals
Legal gate false-positives creating delivery delays for low-risk requests
